how.intro: Adds a real stop order on SoDEX for every trade, as a safety net if DeskLabs goes offline.
steps: It is placed as soon as the entry fills, 0.1% of the price further away than the bot's own stop loss, so normally the bot's stop acts first.
Once the trade is far enough in profit (see Move stop to break-even), the stop on SoDEX moves to break-even, then follows the price to lock in profit.
how.note: It is triggered by the mark price and closes the whole position at market.

vfEarlyFees.label: Early profit
vfEarlyFees.hint: Exit early once the price gain reaches this many times the round-trip fee (1–20×)

how.intro: Takes a smaller profit early instead of waiting for the full hold time.
steps: After the delay set next to it (seconds), if profit ≥ this × the round-trip fees, the bot closes the trade.
Example: 3× with 10 s → after 10 seconds, any trade that has made 3 times its fees is closed.
how.note: Lower = more small wins, less time exposed. Higher = lets winners run longer.

vfEarlySecs.label: Early profit after
vfEarlySecs.hint: Seconds in the trade before an early exit is allowed

maxOrders.label: Max open position, in orders
maxOrders.hint: How many orders’ worth of position the bot may hold, 1–10. 1 = at most one order size (20 USDC at 20 per side); at the limit the bot only posts the close.

how.intro: Caps how much position the bot may build, as a number of orders: max position = order size per side × this number.
steps: While under the cap, the bot keeps quoting both sides.
With a position open, the side that would add to it moves further away (2–3 ticks back), and the side that closes it stays near the price.
At the cap, the side that would add more stops quoting until the position shrinks.
how.note: Example: 20 USDC per side and 1 order → at most about 20 USDC of position at a time. Higher values give more fills but more price risk.

quoteLevel.label: Quote position in the order book
quoteLevel.hint: 0 = at the best bid and ask (one tick inside when the spread is wide), the fastest fills. 1, 2… = that many price steps behind: fewer fills, less exposure to fast moves. Works the same on every market because it follows the live order book.

how.intro: Sets where your bid and ask sit in the SoDEX order book, counted in ticks (the smallest price step) from the best price.
steps: 0: your bid sits at the best bid and your ask at the best ask. If the gap between them is 3 ticks or more, the bot goes 1 tick inside it to be first in line.
1, 2, 3…: each step moves both quotes 1 tick further from the best price.
Your bid is always below your ask, so the bot never trades with itself.
how.note: Lower = more fills and volume, but more fills right before the price moves against you. Higher = fewer fills and less volume. Because it counts ticks, the same value works on every market.

vfStopMove.label: Move stop to break-even at
vfStopMove.hint: When the price gain reaches this many times the break-even fee (entry fee + market exit fee + slippage), the stop on SoDEX moves to break-even. From 2 more, it locks in profit and follows the best price. Lower moves sooner but small swings can close the trade.

how.intro: When to move the stop on SoDEX to break-even, in multiples of G. G = entry fee + taker exit fee + a little slippage: the price move needed just to cover costs.
steps: Profit reaches this × G: the stop moves to break-even (fees included), so the trade can no longer lose.
Profit reaches (this + 2) × G: the stop locks in profit and follows the best price, 2 × G behind it.
The stop never moves back.
how.note: Lower (e.g. 1–1.5) protects sooner but gets stopped at break-even more often. Higher leaves more room. The current target price is shown in Decisions when the stop is placed.

smartQuoting.label: Smart quoting
smartQuoting.hint: Prices quotes from the Binance futures price, follows the live SoDEX order book, keeps unchanged quotes in place, and cuts a position at market when the price runs 15 bp against it. Lower cost per $1M, fewer fills. Turn it off for faster volume.

how.intro: Normally the bot keeps one bid and one ask at the set position in the order book and replaces them every refresh. With Smart quoting on:
steps: Binance price: the bot follows the Binance futures price of the same coin, converted to SoDEX with the usual gap between the two. A quote that adds to your position is never placed more than 0.5 bp past that price (no ask below it, no bid above it).
Pulled on a move: if the Binance price moves through a resting quote that adds to your position, the bot pulls it at once and quotes again.
Quotes stay in place: a quote whose price and size haven't changed is kept instead of being cancelled and placed again, so it keeps its place in the queue.
Live order book: when the best SoDEX price moves away from a quote that adds to your position, that quote moves with it right away (at most every 1.5 seconds) instead of waiting for the next refresh.

Cut on a run: if the Binance price moves 15 bp or more against your open position, the bot cancels its orders and closes the position at market. A closing order that only waits in the book can't catch a price that keeps running.
Warm-up: for the first 6 seconds both quotes sit 2 bp further away until there is enough price data.
Lopsided book: one side of the top 10 levels holds at least 2× the other. The thin side steps back 1 bp (e.g. heavy bids → the ask steps back).
A lopsided-book step-back is kept for 15 seconds after the last trigger. Orders that close your inventory always stay at the best price.
how.note: Binance leads SoDEX by about a quarter of a second, and a large SoDEX maker picks off small quotes right after Binance moves; Smart quoting avoids standing in its way. Expect fewer fills in exchange for a lower cost per $1M; turn it off when you need volume faster. Markets not listed on Binance futures skip the Binance steps. Works only when quotes follow the order book (Quote level). Pulled quotes, cuts and the number of requests sent to SoDEX each minute are logged in Decisions. Beta: thresholds may change.

riskDisclosure.title: Risk Disclosure
riskDisclosure.warnTitle: Read this before you start a bot.
riskDisclosure.warnBody: Every DeskLabs bot trades real funds on SoDEX mainnet. You can lose part or all of the money a bot uses, and with leverage you can lose it fast. Only use money you can afford to lose.

loss.title: Real money, real losses
loss.body: Digital asset prices move quickly and without warning. An automated bot follows its rules whatever the market does: it keeps buying in a falling market or selling in a rising one if that is what its settings say. DeskLabs does not guarantee any profit and does not predict prices.

leverage.title: Leverage and liquidation
leverage.body: Futures Grid, Futures DCA, Funding Arbitrage and perps TWAP use perpetual contracts. With leverage, a small price move against you becomes a large loss. If your margin falls below SoDEX’s maintenance requirement, SoDEX can liquidate your position. A liquidation happens on SoDEX and DeskLabs cannot stop or reverse it.

margin.title: Multi-Asset Margin
margin.body: In cross margin, SoDEX counts non-USDC assets as margin at a collateral ratio below 100%, so they are worth less as margin than their full value. Losses are settled in USDC. Your USDC balance can go negative, and an account can be liquidated even without an open position. Isolated margin uses USDC only. The Portfolio page shows how much of your balance counts as margin.

sharedLeverage.title: Shared leverage per market
sharedLeverage.body: On SoDEX, leverage and margin mode are set per account and per market. When a bot sets leverage on a market, it changes it for your whole account, including trades you place yourself. DeskLabs blocks the start when that would affect an open position, and asks you to confirm otherwise.

items.grid: Grid: if price leaves your range, the grid has no levels left to trade and you hold what it bought, or the short it opened, at a loss.
items.dca: DCA: extra buys add to a losing position. A long fall uses all of them and the loss grows with every one.
items.recurring: Recurring Buy: keeps buying on schedule and never sells, whatever the price.
items.rebalancing: Rebalancing: sells assets that rose and buys ones that fell; in a long trend this can lag simply holding.
items.funding: Funding Arbitrage: funding rates change and can turn negative; the spot and perp legs can drift apart; the perp leg can be liquidated.
items.twap: TWAP: slices still pay the spread and can fill at worse prices than when you started.

backtest.title: Backtests and suggestions
backtest.body: A backtest replays SoDEX price history with modeled fills. It is a simulation, not a forecast, and real fills, fees and slippage differ. Strategy plans and AI parameters come from rule-based software reading your data. They are not advice and can be wrong for future markets.

items.offline: SoDEX, networks or DeskLabs can be slow or offline. Bots may miss orders, and open orders stay on SoDEX while that lasts.
items.unknown: When an order’s result is unknown, DeskLabs checks with SoDEX before acting again, which can delay the bot.
items.key: If your SoDEX connection expires or stops working, bots pause until you reconnect.
items.bugs: Software can have bugs. Server-enforced risk limits reduce, but do not remove, that risk.

costs.title: Costs
costs.body: Bots that trade often pay SoDEX trading fees and the {fee} DeskLabs builder fee on many fills. Perpetual positions pay or receive funding. These costs can turn a small gain into a loss.

items.revoke: Turn off the builder fee or disconnect SoDEX in Settings to stop DeskLabs trading entirely.

spot_grid.what: Places buy orders below the price and sell orders above it, and earns small gains as the price moves up and down.

futures_grid.what: Works like a grid on a perpetual, using leverage. Gains and losses are both larger.
futures_grid.lose: A fast move can hit the loss limit quickly. Funding fees also apply.

spot_dca.what: Buys, then buys more as the price drops, and sells the whole position at a take-profit.
spot_dca.lose: A long fall uses every extra buy and can reach the loss limit.

futures_dca.what: Adds to a perpetual position as the price moves against it, then takes profit. Uses leverage.
futures_dca.lose: A trend that keeps going can hit the stop loss. Funding fees also apply.

recurring_buy.what: Buys a small amount every week, whatever the price. It never sells.
recurring_buy.lose: If the price falls for a long time, your holdings fall with it.

rebalancing.what: Keeps your coins at a fixed mix by trimming what grew and adding to what fell.
rebalancing.lose: If all your coins fall together, your total value falls too.

funding_arb.what: Holds the coin and an equal perpetual short to collect funding payments.
funding_arb.lose: Funding turns negative, or the two sides drift apart before the bot closes them.

calc.title: How these numbers are calculated
calc.volBody: Data: SoDEX 1-minute price candles. For each minute we take the gap between its highest and lowest price, as a share of the price, in basis points (bp; 1 bp = 0.01%). For each hour of each day we take the middle value (median) of its 60 minutes and compare it with the median of the whole day. An hour counts as hot on a day when it is more than 2× that day’s median.
calc.costBody: Data: public trades on SoDEX. After each trade we look at the price 30 seconds later: if it moved against the side whose order was resting in the book (the maker), that is the cost in bp. Spread is the gap between the best buy and sell price, counted in the smallest price steps (ticks). Both are medians per hour.
calc.botsBody: Data: the real fills of live Market Making and Volume Builder bots; practice bots are left out. Markout cost / $1M = fees paid minus the price move on each fill one minute later, per $1M of volume, counting only fills that have a price one minute later. It is a markout estimate, not realised profit or loss. A bot-hour is one bot running for one hour, so 3 bots running for an hour is 3 bot-hours. An hour counts for a bot when it placed at least one order in that hour. Fewer than 3 bot-hours is a Thin sample.
calc.estBody: Est. CPM uses the same model as the Market Making cost card: fees (SoDEX maker fee plus the default Market Making builder fee) plus the price loss the model expects from 1-minute swings, per $1M of volume. Typical day uses the hour's median swing across days. Incl. shock days works out that cost for every day from that day's own swing and takes the average (mean, not median). On days when the hour's largest 15-minute move was {bp} bp or more (when Market Making cuts a position), it adds one position cut: cut cost in bp × 100 × (one cut's size ÷ one Market Making bot's average volume per hour). These are estimates from market data, not a forecast.
calc.cutMeasured: Cut cost: taker fee {taker} bp plus {slip} bp average slippage, measured from {n} real position cuts (fill price against the last 1-minute close before the cut).
calc.cutTakerOnly: Cut cost: taker fee {taker} bp only. There are {n} real position cuts in this period, fewer than the {min} needed to measure slippage.
calc.cutSizeCuts: One cut's size is {ratio}× the bot's order size, the average of those real cuts ({notional} each). A bot-hour fills {fills}× the order size, so one cut is {pct}% of one bot-hour's volume. Source: {source}.
calc.cutSizeRatio: One cut's size is {ratio}× the bot's order size: the median, over live Market Making bots in the last 14 days, of the largest position each bot held (from its fills) divided by its order size. A bot-hour fills {fills}× the order size, so one cut is {pct}% of one bot-hour's volume. Source: {source}.
calc.cutNone: Position cuts not included: no live Market Making bot has volume in the last 14 days to size a cut against. Source: {source}.
calc.calibrated: Est. CPM (estimate) = incl. shock days × {factor}: the median, over {hours} hours with 3 or more bot-hours of live Market Making bots in the last 14 days, of the bots' Markout cost / $1M divided by the incl. shock days estimate for that hour. Source: {source}.
calc.calibratedDefault: Est. CPM (estimate) = incl. shock days × {factor}. Source: {source}.
calc.cpm: CPM = cost per $1M of volume. Est. CPM is an estimate from market data; Markout cost is measured from bot fills one minute later.

help.medianBp: Typical size of one minute's price swing in this hour: (high − low) of each 1-minute candle as a share of price, middle value across the period. 1 bp = 0.01%.
help.p90Bp: A rough minute in this hour: 9 out of 10 minutes swung less than this.

rules.title: What counts as a news signal
rules.sub: Rules v{v} · a starting guess that the results prove or drop
rules.intro: A signal is one story about one SoDEX asset, of a type on the list below. The type sets the direction; Claude only names the type and the asset. The bot decides on the first article and locks the confidence level at that moment. Articles that arrive later don’t open more trades; if they would have raised the level, the trade is tagged “later High” for analysis.
rules.typesTable: News types, direction and max hold

rows.etf: ETF approved / ETF delayed or denied
rows.regulator: Regulator acts against a project / rules in its favour
rows.treasury: Company buys the token for its treasury / sells it
rows.earnings: Earnings beat or raised guidance / miss or cut (stock markets)
rows.unlock: Token unlock over 2% of supply within 7 days
rows.notSignals: Not signals: partnerships, price analysis and opinion, macro data (macro goes to the risk filter)

rules.tiers:
Source tiers

Top: the primary source itself (exchange, company, regulator, ETF issuer), Bloomberg, Reuters.

Mid: established crypto media and verified founders or executives.

Low: aggregators, anonymous and influencer accounts.
rules.tiersNote: The full list of SoSoValue source names is kept in the rules and versioned with them.
rules.tpsl:
Take profit and stop loss

TP = 1.5 × and SL = 0.75 × the asset’s typical move over the max hold (from its last 30 days). If TP is under 2× the cost of a trade, the signal is skipped.

when.high: 2 or more independent sources already at the first decision, at least one top-tier, nothing contradicting
when.medium: One top-tier source, or 2 or more mid-tier sources
when.low: A single mid- or low-tier source

rules.firstAnswer: When do we get a first answer? The main test pools all news signals: about 100 closed trades, so 3–4 weeks at the current ~30 a week. Results by level or news type are a second look, once each has 30 or more trades. Once there is an average, the page shows how many trades it really needs; a small edge needs more than 100.
rules.passIf: A level passes only if it also beats random entries at the same moments, with the same long / short mix, TP, SL and max hold. A rising market makes long news look good; the random comparison takes that out.
